claims.claim: Historical model: content-addressed source objects, input-addressed ordinary outputs, and fixed-output derivations have distinct identities. Input identity does not establish equal realized bytes; extensional equality is an explicit model assumption.
claims.evidence: Supplied phd-thesis.pdf, PDF105-106/printed97-98 section5.3; PDF108-114/printed100-106 section5.4; PDF142/printed134 section5.7. https://nixos.org/~eelco/pubs/phd-thesis.pdf

claims.claim: Historical canonical encoding records regular-file bytes/executability, ordered directory entries and symlink targets, excluding timestamps and most metadata; namespace and symbolic name participate in store identity.

Validity, stored-content hash, closure and reverse-reference integrity are explicit invariants. Per-output locks, a second validity check, successful output validation and transactional registration support concurrent retry. Power-loss recovery additionally depends on filesystem durability.
claims.evidence: PDF103-108/printed95-100, Invariants1-4 and Figures5.3-5.4; PDF119-121/printed111-113, realization steps75-82

claims.claim: Runtime references are found against the full input closure. Encoded, compressed, hidden and outside-store references limit conservative scanning; the author's positive result is empirical for the studied Unix packages.
claims.evidence: PDF65-67/printed57-59 section3.4; PDF113-114/printed105-106; PDF121-122/printed113-114, Figure5.12; PDF187-188/printed179-180

claims.claim: Root registration must be coordinated with GC before unprotected objects can be used; in-flight operations need temporary roots. Interrupted collection must invalidate/delete referrers before their dependencies. The historical proof excludes nontrivial reference cycles and does not automatically protect executing programs through profiles alone.
claims.evidence: PDF133-142/printed125-134, sections5.6.1-5.6.4; specifically PDF138/printed130 Figure5.21 and PDF134-135/printed126-127 discussion of running Firefox

claims.claim: The intensional content-addressed output model is labeled a rough prototype. Self references require hash-modulo-self and rewriting; output content addressing changes realization lookup from one predicted output to potentially multiple content results.

Bootstrap tools enter as retained atoms, while compiler/libc isolation, platform libraries, dynamic loaders and RPATH policy remain package-system responsibilities. Rust manager portability cannot establish binary portability.
claims.evidence: PDF177-179/printed169-171 section7.1; PDF185-188/printed177-180 section7.1.2-7.1.4. Last sentence is design inference.

findings.coverage: PDF1-15, motivation, binary patches, patch chaining, base selection and experience; sections1-6 and conclusion opening. Supplied body has no printed page numbers.

claims.claim: Changes to fundamental inputs propagate through build identities and require dependent rebuilds. Binary patches reduce transfer cost while constructing a new output; they do not eliminate rebuilds or justify destructive in-place upgrades.

Canonical archive deltas handle directory renames; a weighted graph selects patch/download chains, with full-download fallback and source-archive hash checking. Patch-base selection remains heuristic.

Results cover 50 historical releases and selected comparisons, with CPU/memory costs and separate disk duplication. They do not establish current or Kedra performance. Defer deltas until correct full transfer is qualified.
claims.evidence: PDF13-14 section5 and Table1; final recommendation is design inference

findings.coverage: PDF3-9/printed81-87 and PDF13/printed91: implementation, frontend separation, substitutes, user environment policy and limitations

claims.claim: A simpler store-expression intermediate representation separates evolving frontend languages from realization and deployment policy, allowing alternative frontends.

Immutable installation space and user-selected environment views are separate. Substitution realizes the same requested object through another mechanism, and build-only inputs need not be transferred with binary runtime closures.

A renamed profile pointer and retained generation roots support atomic selection and rollback. This does not establish atomic process restart or mutable-data rollback, and the conclusion's secure multi-user sharing is described as future work.
claims.evidence: PDF9/printed87 User Environment Policies; PDF13/printed91 Conclusion. Process/data limitation is design inference from scope of mechanism.

findings.coverage: PDF3-9 sections3-8. Supplied body has no printed page numbers.

claims.claim: Build-time consumption, retained references and runtime-supplied composition are distinct dependencies; deployment requires the transitive closure of retained references.

Recognizable hash names support conservative scanning, but UTF-16, compressed pointers and non-store dependencies can escape it. The reported 135-component experience and 47-package comparison are bounded empirical evidence, not a completeness theorem.
Relocation can invalidate embedded pointers and checksums. Stable namespaces help sharing; language-independent implementation is not proof of ABI or filesystem portability.

claims.claim: The paper describes Maak, a Haskell prototype, integrating explicit cross-package build graphs, activation and prebuilt-derivate reuse; it is not a modern Nix implementation description.

Maak's update barriers suppress selected dependency propagation; its collision strategy can overwrite/rebuild derivates. These differ from strict immutable content/recipe contracts and must not be adopted as if equivalent.
claims.evidence: PDF11-12, Barriers and section5 Implementation; recommendation is design inference

claims.claim: Sharing security, binary-only support and scalability are stated future work.

findings.coverage: 2021 announcement; revision-pinned README, architecture design, workspace/tree and selected actual Rust interfaces. No original-depot equivalence, complete audit, build, runtime or independent CI qualification.

claims.claim: The 2021 announcement proposes nixpkgs compatibility and modular evaluator/builder/store design; these are historical goals.

The pinned README declares unstable APIs and non-production readiness, lists store/build components, and declares GPL-3.0 code with MIT protocol definitions. Its Nix2.3 statement concerns Nix builds of Tvix, not complete package compatibility.
claims.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tvlfyi/tvix/9bed4ce6fc4c308f28df485b286a9aee467af686/README.md , warning, Components, Compatibility and License structure

claims.claim: Actual pinned tree/workspace omit build/castore/store, despite the README inventory. Architecture prose acknowledges outdated statements. Actual TvixStoreIO delegates language IO to SimulatedStoreIO.

The simulated store computes NAR path identities and maps imports to source paths; it can read existing local Nix store paths despite the header's stronger purity description. It provides no realization engine. Independent purity requires an explicit allowed-input adapter.
claims.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tvlfyi/tvix/9bed4ce6fc4c308f28df485b286a9aee467af686/simstore/src/lib.rs lines1-16,116-141,254-277; final sentence is design inference

claims.claim: Inspected nix-compat interfaces implement typed derivations, canonical ATerm serialization and Nix input/fixed-output path calculations. StorePath and fingerprints assume /nix/store. These are potential compatibility components, not a ready generic runtime engine.
EvalIO provides injectable language-level filesystem operations, not a complete realization protocol. Suitability for Kedra reuse remains unqualified without an end-to-end experiment.

handoffs.why_relevant: O3 owns modern semantics. Reconcile historical input/fixed/content addressing, runtime roots, root acquisition, reference-set trust and NAR metadata limits; O1 did not analyze this manual.
O2 owns OS activation. Preserve separation of store/profile pointer atomicity from running-service transition and mutable-state rollback; O1 did not analyze this manual.
